narrator.instruct: Gripping, energetic storyteller telling an astonishing true sea adventure, brisk and excited, never calm.

sailor.instruct: A rough, exhausted fifteenth-century sailor at sea, angry and desperate, shouting at his captain.

lookout.instruct: A young sailor high in the rigging at night, suddenly seeing land, bursting with joy, shouting at the top of his lungs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Columbus lied to his own crew about how far they'd sailed. It still almost wasn't enough.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: September, fourteen ninety-two. Three small ships sail west from the Canary Islands.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You see, Columbus keeps two counts of distance: a true one, and a shorter one for the crew, so they won't panic.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: October tenth. The crew has had enough.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His log, known only from a friar's summary, says he calmed them. Some later writers say he made a deal: three more days.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next day, the sea sends clues. A carved stick. A branch with berries.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Two in the morning, October twelfth, a lookout shouts.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now, what if they had turned back? Someone else would almost certainly have crossed. Portugal reached Brazil in fifteen hundred.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But this crossing started the great swap. Potatoes and chocolate went east. Smallpox went west, and with war and slavery, killed most of the Americas' native people.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A lie, one tense night, and a few twigs. That's how close they came to turning around.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the lookout's reward? Columbus said he'd seen a light first, and kept it.
